subject: Urgent: p95 surge for model-2.7c — request for emergency variant fallback
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jared Lee <jared.lee@opticore.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: p95 surge for model-2.7c — request for emergency variant fallback

Marcus / Laura / Jared —

We're seeing a sharp p95 latency increase for OptiCore traffic on model-2.7c starting ~15:50 PST. Key signal: production p95 jumped from 210ms to 640ms (30-minute window), error rate steady but user visible latency is causing timeouts in their reconciliation flows. OptiCore is reporting timeouts on batch jobs and a downstream ticket has been opened by their ops team.

Quick facts:
- affected model: model-2.7c (quantized v2)
- impacted routes: /v1/generate (OptiCore account routing rule)
- p95: 210ms -> 640ms (delta +430ms)
- traffic share: OptiCore is ~22% of model-2.7c requests in us-west region right now

We need an emergency mitigation: flip OptiCore traffic to the warm variant model-2.7b-fast (compatible decoder, slightly higher cost but much lower p95 historically) while SRE investigates root cause. Marcus — can you confirm the traffic-split override and estimated time-to-cutover?

I've attached a p95 chart and the canary logs snapshot. Jared — I realize this is bad timing; if you confirm you're seeing the same failures on your side we'll proceed with the fallback and open an SLA exception for any customer-visible SLO misses.

Ask: Marcus to initiate variant fallback and confirm rollback plan. Laura to approve emergency SLA exception/credits if needed so we can proceed without legal delay.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: p95-trend-20261129.png, canary-logs-20261129.zip

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Jared Lee <jared.lee@opticore.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 16:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: p95 surge for model-2.7c — request for emergency variant fallback

On Sun, Nov 29, 2026 at 16:12, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marcus / Laura / Jared —
> We're seeing a sharp p95 latency increase for OptiCore traffic on model-2.7c...

Thanks Priyom — I've started a quick triage. Initial findings from the canary logs:
- I see increased kernel queueing on two gpus in the us-west pool serving model-2.7c (node ids gw-14 and gw-15).
- KV-cache hit rates are unchanged; the extra latency looks like a scheduling/frag issue after the recent quantized kernel update (rolled 2026-11-28 02:00 UTC).

Mitigation options:
1) Emergency variant fallback: split OptiCore traffic to model-2.7b-fast (recommended). Cutover ETA ~6-10 minutes; risk: slightly higher per-token cost, minimal inference quality delta.
2) Immediate canary revert of the kernel change on gw-14/gw-15 — ETA ~20-35 minutes, higher blast radius and requires manual kernel swap + service restart.

If we are to proceed with option 1, I will:
- create a one-off traffic-split override in the routing layer for OptiCore
- run a 5-minute verification canary and keep split for 1 hour while I collect logs
- prepare a controlled rollback plan (no-model-variant-downtime) to return traffic once SLOs stable

Laura — I need your explicit approval on the SLA exception / customer credits so we can act immediately (Procurement may require the signed SLA-exception form). If approved, I'll proceed with the variant fallback now.

Attachments referenced: canary-logs-20261129.zip

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Jared Lee <jared.lee@opticore.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@opticore.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: p95 surge for model-2.7c — request for emergency variant fallback

Priyom / Marcus —

We are definitely seeing timeouts on our reconciliation jobs (batch window failing the SLA). Appreciate the rapid triage. Option 1 (variant fallback) sounds safest to get us back to acceptable latency. Please proceed.

A couple of notes from our side:
- Procurement will need an official SLA-exception document for any service credit; I attached the internal request and have flagged Legal to expect a DocuSign.
- Can you provide an ETA for full recovery and a short note we can send to our ops team about what changed? The ops team is currently holding all dependent jobs until we get sign-off.

If you proceed with the fallback, please confirm: expected p95 after cutover and estimated duration you'll keep the override in place.

Thanks,
Jared
Jared Lee
Head of Engineering Operations, OptiCore Financial
jared.lee@opticore.com

Attachments: OptiCore_SLA_Request_Nov29.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Lee <jared.lee@opticore.com>, Legal <legal@redwood.ai>, CS <cs@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: p95 surge for model-2.7c — request for emergency variant fallback

Marcus / Priyom —

Authorize the emergency variant fallback to model-2.7b-fast for OptiCore. Marcus, proceed with the traffic-split override and complete the 5-minute canary verification. Keep me updated with the verification metrics (p50/p95 and error rate) and confirm when traffic is fully stable.

On the SLA exception/credits front: we will offer OptiCore a temporary credit (5% of last month's usage) for the window of degraded latency and complete the SLA-exception form. Legal and Procurement are cc'd — Priyom, please coordinate the signed DocuSign and confirm once received so we can close the loop.

Also: open a post-incident RCA and circulate within 72 hours. Marcus, include kernel rollout timeline, canary behavior, and recommended mitigations (hotfix vs. revert cadence). CS to coordinate customer comms.

Laura
